title: Virtualization: Hypervisors, VMs and Containers
oneLiner: Type 1 and type 2 hypervisors, hardware-assisted virtualization, VMs versus containers, snapshots, templates, live migration, overcommit and thin provisioning.
keyTakeaway: A hypervisor shares one machine's hardware among VMs that each run their own OS; containers share the host's kernel and isolate only processes, so they're lighter but a weaker boundary. Snapshots are for quick rollback, not backups, and overcommitted CPU, memory or thin disks work until everyone needs them at once.
explanation:
Nearly every server you'll work on is a virtual machine, whether in a company's VMware cluster or a cloud. This lesson explains what a hypervisor does, how VMs differ from containers, and the features that make VMs easy to manage: snapshots, templates and live migration.

It also covers overcommit and thin provisioning, which explain both why virtualization is cheap and how a busy host or a full datastore slows or stops every VM on it.
